Users who are used to using ChatGPT for quick image searches can now use a brand-new gesture to add photos to conversations even faster. Let's take a look at how to use it.

ChatGPT makes it easier for users to attach recently taken photos to conversations

Although the Visual Intelligence feature on iOS has been available for nearly two years, it currently only supports newer iPhone models and is not available in all regions.

For users who rely on ChatGPT for similar visual searches, attaching images in the past required tapping the "+" button, selecting "Photos," and then picking the right picture from the album.

Although this process is not too complicated, OpenAI has simplified it slightly this week, allowing users to add their most recent photos to a conversation with a convenient new gesture.

OpenAI's Adam Fry said on X that users can now long-press the "+" button to the left of the input box to instantly bring up the last four photos taken.

Users can choose one of these photos to attach to the conversation, and then ask a question or include it as part of the prompt.

This new gesture is one of several ChatGPT improvements this week. Other updates include a more accurate grasp of the current time, improved loading and execution speeds for long conversations on the web version, and clearer interface prompts when users are waiting for a network connection.

Have you used AI for visual search? Let us know in the comments section.
